references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the sending out of the twelve, where Jesus commissions them to preach that the kingdom of heaven is near and to heal the sick – the same dual commission as in Luke 9:2.
Mark's parallel account of the sending out of the twelve. Jesus sends them out two by two with authority, and they preach and heal, which corresponds directly to Luke 9:2.
Jesus sends out the seventy(-two) with the same type of commission: to preach that the kingdom of God has come near and to heal the sick. This expands the commission from Luke 9:2 to a larger group.
Jesus himself went around preaching the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease among the people. The twelve are sent out with the same commission that Jesus himself carried out.

Jesus says that he must preach the kingdom of God also in the other towns, for that is why he was sent. The preaching of the kingdom of God is the core mission that he passes on to his disciples in 9:2.
The preceding verse where Jesus gathers the twelve and gives them power and authority over all evil spirits and to heal diseases – the prerequisite for the commission in verse 2.
The fulfillment of the commission given in verse 2: the disciples went out and traveled from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing everywhere.

Paul in Rome preached the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ. The preaching of the kingdom of God continues as an apostolic mission, in line with what Jesus gave his disciples in Luke 9:2.
Jesus went around in all the towns and villages, teaching in the synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease – a model for the commission he gave to the twelve.
The prophecy that the Lord's Spirit is upon the anointed one to preach good news and proclaim freedom – the messianic mission that Jesus passes on to his disciples in Luke 9:2.
